questions_and_answers.question_text: What is a mǔ in hectares?

articles.text:
7. A: Hē! Nǐmende càidì shōude bù    Wow! You've harvested quite a lot from
      shǎo a!                        your vegetable plots!
   B: Jiù shi ma, měimǔ dì dōu shōu Sure, we harvested over ten thousand
      yíwànduō jīn na!               catties from each mǔ of land!

Notes on No. 7

càidì: "vegetable plots" or "vegetable fields" (large or small).

shōu: "to harvest"

Shōubudào liángshi, zěnme chī    If we can't harvest any grain, how will
fàn ne?                          we eat? (a rhetorical question said by
                                 farmers when working in the fields)

mǔ: A Chinese unit of area equal to 1/15 HECTARE. In English this is simply written mu.

dì: "land," "ground," or "fields"

Zhèikuài dì yǐqián shi wǒ        This piece of land used to belong to my
fùqinde.                         father.
Zhème zǎo nǐmen jiù dào dìli qù  You're going to work in the fields so
gōngzuò la!                      early!

shōude bù shǎo: "harvested quite a lot." Here are more examples of the pattern VERB + -DE + QUANTITY:

Nǐ chīde tài shǎo.               You're eating too little.
Guānyú zhèige, wǒ zhīdaode bù    I don't know much about this.
duō.
Tā kàn xiǎoshuō kànde bǐ wǒ duō. He reads more fiction than I.
Nǐ mǎide tài duō le!             You bought too much!
